_comment: Marker layout for the clay block's base plate.
Coordinates are metres in the BOARD frame: origin at the centre of the
plate, x right, y up the plate, z out of its face. The pose this produces
is the pose of that origin, so put the origin where you want the clay
volume anchored — the centre of the seat the block sits in.
Why four markers and not one: four coplanar corners is the minimum for a
pose and the worst case for stability. A single small marker suffers the
planar ambiguity, where two quite different orientations reproject almost
identically and the solver flips between them a few times a second. Spread
several markers across a rigid plate and the corners stop being one small
square, which removes the ambiguity and survives a hand covering part of
the plate.
Why the plate and not the clay: clay deforms and picks up slip. A marker
stuck to the part being sculpted stops being planar, stops being clean, and
is exactly where the user's hands are. The plate is rigid, stays visible,
and is what the block's pose is actually defined against.
Print at 100% scale and MEASURE a printed marker with calipers before
trusting 'size' — printer scaling of a few percent maps straight into a
few percent range error, which at 0.5 m is over a centimetre.
Dictionary: DICT_4X4_50. Generate with
python3 -c "import cv2;cv2.imwrite('m0.png',cv2.aruco.generateImageMarker(cv2.aruco.getPredefinedDictionary(cv2.aruco.DICT_4X4_50),0,600))"
